title: Source-grounded verification of the biogenic-magnetite and alpha-ERD [R] claims in OTA-FND-0024 (Wang et al. 2019 eNeuro; Kirschvink et al. 1992) against the primary neuroscience literature
question: Verify the [R]-marked neurophysiological claims that form the neurological mechanism of OTA-FND-0024-2026-DE against the primary sources. (a) Does the Caltech study (Wang et al. 2019, eNeuro) on alpha-ERD from rotation of earth-strength magnetic fields exist as cited, and does it support the specific claims: rotation of ~35 microtesla (earth-strength) fields triggering event-related desynchronization with 'up to 60%' alpha-amplitude (8-13 Hz) reduction, and subjects reporting no subjective perception? What effect magnitude and participant subgrouping did the paper actually report, and has the result been independently replicated or critiqued in the subsequent human-magnetoreception literature? (b) Are biogenic magnetite (Fe3O4) nanocrystals of 19-24 nm documented in human brain neurons and astrocytes per Kirschvink et al. 1992 (PNAS) and follow-ups, or does the primary record report different size distributions (single-domain ~50 nm vs superparamagnetic smaller crystals), and how has interpretation evolved (endogenous biomineralization vs exogenous/pollution-derived magnetite, e.g., Maher et al. 2016)? (c) What is the current scientific status of human geomagnetic transduction - established, contested, or preliminary - and is the [T] extrapolation from the chain's local field to a similar alpha-ERD cascade physically constrained (field strength, gradient, exposure geometry)?
why_now: The document's central premise - a magnetic chain rewiring a brain before science can detect it - rests entirely on these [R] anchors, and OTA-SCI-0060 (biogenic magnetite and alpha-ERD) is scheduled as an ausstehend companion. The 'up to 60% alpha drop' and '19-24 nm' figures are specific enough to verify against the primary sources, and human geomagnetic transduction is a live, contested area where a freshness check of replication status is warranted.
real_world_anchor: Wang et al. 2019 eNeuro geomagnetic alpha-ERD study; Kirschvink et al. 1992 PNAS biogenic magnetite in human brain; subsequent human magnetoreception literature (Maher et al. 2016 and later replications/critiques).
novelty_reason: No prior OTA research topic covers biogenic magnetite in the human brain or geomagnetic alpha-ERD transduction. RES-20260823-5BEB27E7 audits mtDNA/biophoton/piRNA anchors of the Lambda-haplogroup system (a different novel and different biological substrates), not brain magnetite or EEG alpha desynchronization, so this is a distinct, unaddressed gap.
